stage_a_public.question: Proposition P: for every natural number k and all real-coefficient polynomials p and q, if both have degree at most 2k+1, and all their ordinary derivatives of orders 0 through k agree at -1 and agree at 0, then p=q. Is P valid under the assumptions and conventions below?
assumptions: k is an arbitrary natural number, including zero; p and q are arbitrary real-coefficient polynomials, including the zero polynomial.
For every natural j with 0≤j≤k, the j-th ordinary derivatives of p and q agree at -1 and also agree at 0.
Both p and q have degree at most 2k+1 under the stated zero-polynomial convention.
conventions: The derivative of order zero is the polynomial itself, so j=0 requires equal endpoint values.
The degree bound means ordinary degree for nonzero polynomials, and the zero polynomial is admitted.
Equality in the conclusion is equality of polynomials, not equality only at the endpoints. No prescribed numerical endpoint values or interpolant existence assumption is supplied.

gold_private.formal_challenge_target: ∀ (k : ℕ) (p q : Polynomial ℝ), p.natDegree ≤ 2 * k + 1 → q.natDegree ≤ 2 * k + 1 → (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval (-1) = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval (-1)) → (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval 0 = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval 0) → p = q
gold_private.reference_proof:
by
  have qcb_step_jet104_jet_iff : ∀ (p q : Polynomial ℝ) (a : ℝ) (k : ℕ), (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval a = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval a) ↔ (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ (k + 1) ∣ p - q :=
    by
      intro p q a k
      constructor
      · intro h
        have ht : Polynomial.X ^ (k + 1) ∣ Polynomial.taylor a (p - q) := by
          apply Polynomial.X_pow_dvd_iff.mpr
          intro j hj
          have he : (j.factorial : ℝ) * (Polynomial.taylor a (p - q)).coeff j = 0 := by
            rw [← QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.eval_iterate_derivative]
            simp only [Polynomial.iterate_derivative_sub, Polynomial.eval_sub,
              h j (by omega), sub_self]
          exact (mul_eq_zero.mp he).resolve_left (by exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_ne_zero j)
        have hm := map_dvd (Polynomial.taylorAlgHom (-a)) ht
        simpa [Polynomial.taylor_taylor, ← sub_eq_add_neg] using hm
      · intro h j hj
        exact QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.jet_eq_of_pow_dvd_sub p q a k j hj h
  have qcb_step_jet104_left : ∀ (k : ℕ) (p q : Polynomial ℝ), (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval (-1) = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval (-1)) → QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus k ∣ p - q :=
    by
      intro k p q h
      exact (qcb_step_jet104_jet_iff p q (-1) k).mp h
  have qcb_step_jet104_right : ∀ (k : ℕ) (p q : Polynomial ℝ), (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval 0 = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval 0) → QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus k ∣ p - q :=
    by
      intro k p q h
      exact (qcb_step_jet104_jet_iff p q 0 k).mp h
  have qcb_step_jet104_coprime : ∀ (k : ℕ), IsCoprime (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus k) (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus k) :=
    by
      intro k
      unfold QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus
        QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus
      apply IsCoprime.pow
      exact Polynomial.isCoprime_X_sub_C_of_isUnit_sub (by norm_num)
  have qcb_step_jet104_product : ∀ (k : ℕ) (p q : Polynomial ℝ), (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval (-1) = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval (-1)) → (∀ j ≤ k, (Polynomial.derivative^[j] p).eval 0 = (Polynomial.derivative^[j] q).eval 0) → (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus k) * (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus k) ∣ p - q :=
    by
      intro k p q hl hr
      exact (qcb_step_jet104_coprime k).mul_dvd
        (qcb_step_jet104_left k p q hl) (qcb_step_jet104_right k p q hr)
  have qcb_step_jet104_degree : ∀ (k : ℕ), ((QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus k) * (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus k)).natDegree = 2 * k + 2 :=
    by
      intro k
      unfold QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus
        QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus
      rw [Polynomial.natDegree_mul (pow_ne_zero _ (Polynomial.X_sub_C_ne_zero _))
        (pow_ne_zero _ (Polynomial.X_sub_C_ne_zero _))]
      simp only [Polynomial.natDegree_pow, Polynomial.natDegree_X_sub_C, mul_one]
      omega
  have qcb_step_jet104_annihilate : ∀ (k : ℕ) (d : Polynomial ℝ), d.natDegree ≤ 2 * k + 1 → (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.leftModulus k) * (QuantumBlockEncoding.HermitePolynomial.rightModulus k) ∣ d → d = 0 :=
    by
      intro k d hb hdiv
      by_contra hne
      have hd := Polynomial.natDegree_le_of_dvd hdiv hne
      rw [qcb_step_jet104_degree k] at hd
      omega
  intro k p q hp hq hl hr
  apply sub_eq_zero.mp
  exact qcb_step_jet104_annihilate k (p - q)
    ((Polynomial.natDegree_sub_le p q).trans (max_le hp hq))
    (qcb_step_jet104_product k p q hl hr)
gold_private.reference_answer: P is valid. Set d=p-q. Equality of all ordinary derivatives through k at a point a means that (x-a)^(k+1) divides d: the degree-j Taylor coefficient is d^(j)(a)/j!, and the factorial is nonzero over the reals. Thus (x+1)^(k+1) and x^(k+1) both divide d. The two factors are coprime since x+1 and x differ by the unit1, so their product divides d. This product has degree2k+2, whereas d has degree at most2k+1. A nonzero multiple cannot have smaller degree than its divisor, so d=0 and p=q. If d=0 already, this last conclusion is immediate. The assertion includes k=0 and zero input polynomials; it asserts uniqueness, not existence.

gold_private.reference_answer: P is invalid. For every natural k and every nonzero real c, choose p(x)=c*x^(k+1)*(x+1)^(k+1) and q(x)=0. The polynomial p is nonzero and has exact degree2k+2 because its leading coefficient is c. Each endpoint is a root of multiplicity at least k+1, so every derivative of order0 through k vanishes at both-1 and0. Hence p and q satisfy both degree bounds and both endpoint jet-equality hypotheses, but p≠q. Already k=0,c=1 gives p=x(x+1),q=0. The degree allowance2k+2 permits a nonzero multiple of the two endpoint multiplicity factors; divisibility and coprimality still hold. Restoring both bounds to2k+1 repairs universal uniqueness. More precisely, at allowance2k+2 any two polynomials with equal jets differ by a constant multiple of x^(k+1)*(x+1)^(k+1); the parameterized counterexample exhibits this missing freedom. That final classification is explanatory mathematics, not an additional certified root in this packet.
